# synology_ftp (Resource)

FTP and FTPS service configuration. Omitted settings retain existing values. Destroy does not disable either service.

## Adopt existing settings

Use an initialized project from [Check the NAS connection](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/elephant-evergreen/synology/latest/docs#check-the-nas-connection). Add this import block with your resource address and the ID of the existing DSM object.

```terraform
import {
  to = synology_ftp.main
  id = "ftp"
}
```

1. Add the resource block with the values DSM currently reports. Use the sample configuration as a starting point.
2. Run `terraform plan -out=adopt.tfplan`. For one import, expect `1 to import, 0 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy`. If the plan proposes changes, match the differing arguments to DSM and save a new plan.
3. Run `terraform apply adopt.tfplan` once the saved plan contains only the import. The next `terraform plan` should report `No changes`.

## Example configuration

```terraform
resource "synology_ftp" "main" {
  enabled     = false
  tls_enabled = false
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `enabled` (Boolean) Enable FTP.
- `idle_timeout` (Number) Idle timeout in seconds.
- `maximum_connections_per_client` (Number) Maximum connections per IP address; zero means DSM default/unlimited.
- `passive_port_range` (String) Passive port range in DSM start:end syntax.
- `passive_port_range_enabled` (Boolean) Use a custom passive port range.
- `port` (Number) FTP listening port.
- `tls_enabled` (Boolean) Enable FTPS.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Singleton identity and import identifier: ftp. Destroy only releases Terraform management; it never resets DSM settings.
